title: Client fidelity negotiation and spillover protocol
content:
Purpose and scope

Quick working notes on a client-negotiated fidelity approach that lets upstream callers participate in graceful degradation decisions when we must shed load across regions or model families. Focus is on control-plane signals, routing policy primitives, billing/quotas interactions, and a first-draft operational runbook for multi-region spillover.

Why this?
- We frequently see bursts where the only way to maintain latency SLOs is to reduce output fidelity for some traffic slices rather than dropping requests.
- Allowing callers to opt-in to reduced fidelity (or let us choose automatically within an agreed contract) gives better economic outcomes and fewer 5xx failures for customers.
- Need to formalize API-level signals, in-flight downgrade semantics, and how the control plane coordinates regional spillover and tiered capacity accounting.

Key concepts & vocabulary
- Fidelity profile: named set of generation parameters (model family, token budget, sampling temperature, quantized variant, post-processing rules). Example: fidelity:high -> model:gptx-70b, tokens:1024, top_p:0.95; fidelity:reduced -> model:opt-30b-8q, tokens:512, top_p:0.9.
- Client negotiated flag (client_fidelity_preference): enum {prefer_high, tolerate_reduced, force_exact}. Default: tolerate_reduced.
- Degradation reason codes: {region_capacity_pressure, model_failure, p95_latency_sla_violation, network_partition}.
- Spillover action: {route-to-region, route-to-lower-fidelity-model, queue-with-grace-period, respond-with-dial-tone-summary}.

Control plane signals and decision flow (high level)
1) Telemetry ingestion: per-route metrics (rps, p50/p95 latency, token-rate, error-rate), queue depth and GPU utilization from Dedicated pools, region health markers (control-plane heartbeats).
2) Policy evaluation service: continuous evaluator that maps telemetry -> recommended action per route. Inputs: route config, tenant SLA class, client_fidelity_preference, current inventory.
3) Decision publish: compact signed decision bundle written to routing control plane (kafka/etcd) with TTL and revision id. Routers subscribe and enforce.
4) Enforcement: edge routers apply per-request tagging and may mutate request to target fidelity profile or failover region depending on bundle.

Routing policy primitives (proposal)
- priority_tag: numeric (0..100) used to prioritize tail-latency sensitive traffic when shedding.
- fidelity_buckets: ordered list of fidelity profiles for this route with weights for soft-fallback.
- regional_preference: ordered list of regions with optional max_egress_pct to control cross-region costs.
- exhaust_thresholds: hard numbers for capacity usage (gpu_util >= 92%) that trigger mandatory fallback.
- negotiated_window: duration for which client opt-in holds (e.g., 30m) to avoid thrashing.

Sample small DSL snippet (pseudo)
route: /chat/complete
priority_tag: 70
fidelity_buckets: [high, medium, reduced]
regional_preference: [us-west, us-east, eu-west]{max_egress_pct: 15}
exhaust_thresholds: {gpu_util: 92, queue_len: 1000}
client_fidelity_enforced: true

Model variant considerations
- Each fidelity profile maps to a model family + runtime config. We should maintain compatibility metadata: output-syntax (chat vs text), cost_factor, kv_cache_compatibility_label. This lets the runtime decide whether a mid-request model swap is safe or requires re-invocation.
- Prefer same-architecture lower-capacity variants when possible to reuse KV caches (eg, switching from 70b->65b same-arch) to reduce cold-start token cost.
- Define a "downgrade penalty" score for model swaps to capture quality regression risk; surface it to product/CS for pricing and SLOs.

Tiered capacity accounting and billing interactions
- Capacity pools: reserved (dedicated), burst (shared but priced), and fallback (lowest-cost best-effort).
- When the control plane triggers a downgrade, emit an event into billing pipeline with original_fidelity and applied_fidelity so cost reconciliation can apply credits or adjusted metering.
- Pricing model options to present to customers: 1) flat discount when tolerate_reduced is set, 2) per-token dynamic credit when downgrade occurs, 3) SLA-backed rollback windows for enterprise contracts.

Multi-region spillover patterns
Pattern A — short-term burst (seconds->minutes):
- Prefer local downgrade to reduced fidelity model first.
- If local pool is saturated and cross-region egress within budget, route small fractions (sampled) of traffic to secondary region for p95-sensitive requests.
- Use canary headers to compare fidelity quality across regions; slow ramp for any region-level model variant.

Pattern B — region outage (minutes->hours):
- Switch to long-lived client negotiation windows (e.g., 120m) and escalate route weight to other regions.
- Enforce cross-region egress caps and, if exceeded, move lower-priority tenants to best-effort fallback pool.
- Trigger automatic billing/usage-notice events and customer notifications via the Console.

Operational runbook (first-draft)
- Detection: alert when route p95 latency > configured_slo * 1.3 or when gpu_util > 90% for 5m.
- Assess: run policy-evaluator dry-run to see recommended actions (mutations and spill percentages).
- Announce: automated Slack alert to #platform-ops with decision bundle + reason_code + affected_tenants sample.
- Apply: promote decision (two-step: dry-run -> enforce after 60s) unless an on-call manually blocks.
- Monitor: 5m cadence checks for regressions (quality drop detectable via eval hooks or customer complaints).
- Rollback: if negative quality impact exceeds degrade_threshold (custom per-route), revert and instead start slow regional spillover.
- Postmortem: tag this incident with degrade_reason and list of tenants affected; run focused quality evals on saved prompts.

Telemetry & quality measurement
- Instrument prompt-level fingerprints for eval reruns (anonymized).
- Maintain online A/B comparison for fidelity profiles using a lightweight log-prob delta metric and a human-labeled sample channel for regression detection.
- Expose a per-route fidelity-impact gauge to console (expected_quality_loss_estimate).

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should clients be allowed to request an explicit fidelity profile by name, or only via preferences? (force_exact currently reserved for enterprise only).
- How to price unexpected cross-region spillover economically without disincentivizing resiliency? Need finance input.
- Cold-start cost vs user-perceived latency: how much KV cache compatibility buys us in practice? Require experiments.
- Security/audit: ensure downgrade events are logged with tenant context but never leak prompt contents in telemetry exports.

Next steps and TODOs
- [ ] Spike: run simulation (1-week synthetic traffic) to verify policy-evaluator thresholds and spill percentages (owner: Jonah).
- [ ] UX: Console display mockups for showing current fidelity profile and historical downgrade events (owner: Rina).
- [ ] Billing: proposal for crediting customers on degraded responses (owner: Diego).
- [ ] SRE: add route-level TLDRs to status pages when cross-region spillover is active (owner: SRE team).

Notes to self / rough thinking fragments
- Might want a "graceful-summary" response option that returns a short structured summary when we can't serve full tokens — better than a 200 with low-quality text.
- Consider a per-tenant budget for expensive-fidelity usage that can be consumed quickly but replenished monthly.
- Keep default client_fidelity_preference conservative to avoid surprises; surface test endpoints for customers to opt-in.

References & links
- CONFLUENCE-PIECE-3245: earlier notes on fidelity buckets and model tagging
- JIRA-INF-7821: policy-evaluator prototype ticket
- Slack thread: #platform-routing ts:1723456789 (contains sample headers + canary results)

End of draft.
